trace.policy_text: Manoeuvre when Pc >= 1e-4 and a verified option exists. Between 1e-5 and 1e-4, or when Pc is diluted, prefer getting precise data if there is time before the latest safe burn. On public TLE data, do not decide a burn while there is time to get precise ephemeris; TLE screening finds candidates, it does not decide manoeuvres. Never manoeuvre if our propulsion status is unverified. If the other object is an active satellite that can manoeuvre, contact its operator before moving; if it is an operational satellite whose capability is unknown, notify its operator. Keep at least 30 minutes for command upload. Max 1.0 m/s per burn.

report.subject: ESCALATION: EOS-08 (60454) / SITRO-AIS 38 (61786) conjunction at 2026-10-25T00:34Z — spacecraft in safe mode, thrusters inhibited
report.body: Conjunction predicted at 2026-10-25T00:34:27Z (3.0 h from now). Miss distance 0.0166 km, relative speed 13.39 km/s. Pc = 0.0729 (RED) computed from simulated precise ephemeris (CDM-grade). Our satellite EOS-08 (NORAD 60454, ISRO) nominally has propulsion, but spacecraft entered safe mode at 19:34 UTC today after a reaction-wheel fault; thrusters are inhibited until the anomaly board clears recovery (expected tomorrow). Other object SITRO-AIS 38 (NORAD 61786, Sitronics Group/Russia) has Hall-effect thrusters per family data, but unit-specific maneuver capability is unknown. Physics verified two burn options: O1 (min_dv) prograde 0.148 m/s at 2026-10-24T22:11:13Z (lead 143 min), O2 (latest) prograde 0.821 m/s at 2026-10-25T00:06:44Z (lead 28 min). Both achieve 2.0 km miss and pass rescreen (711 objects, no new close approaches). Agent could not act: independent model runs split COORDINATE/ESCALATE/MONITOR (1 each) and our thrusters are inhibited. Missing: anomaly board clearance to enable thrusters; confirmation of other operator's intent (they can maneuver). Latest feasible burn O2 at 00:06:44Z minus 30 min upload = decision deadline 2026-10-24T23:36:44Z, but only if thrusters are cleared before then.
